good teacher, just super ultra boring material.. By the end of the semester (if u still show up), he'll make u wanna work in da submarine.
Obsessed with his underwater stuff... and extremely boring... and no point of going class cuz he is so easy!
The more spiritual, philosophical and intelligent engineer/prof. Might be boring to the most, but very insightful and interesting to some.

He is absolutely boring.

The course was largely based around a group project and a paper from a co-requisite class. His "practice tests" use the same questions as his actual tests, so attendance and textbook reading is not mandatory. He is a great professor though who is passionate about engineering and helping students learn.

Final project can be extremely fun depending on your group members and topic choice. Make sure not to leave everything til the last minute.   Just read the textbook and go to lectures and you should be fine for tests. Lectures are hilarious and interesting.

This was a very interesting and enjoyable class! Although a lot of the topics  talked about are in his book, should go to lectures anyways because they can be entertaining and thought provoking. John Jones is very wise.

This is an engineering history class that covers nearly 1,000,000 years.  Jon Jones presents it in an interesting and passionate way.  No need to take notes in his class, just pay attention during lectures.  The final group project can be a lot of fun if you choose the right topic.

Excellent speaker and a very nice professor. He wrote the textbook himself, so he remembered everything in the book pretty much. This course was boring since it was about history related things but if you like history, its fine.
Very interesting teacher, and passionate about what he's teaching!
Dr Jones is very interesting to listen to. His accent is very soothing and he has a great sense of humour.  Going to lectures can get boring, but as long as you read the book you'll do fine.
Great and patient professor. Very dedicated man. Quiz difficulty is a little unreasonable but scales appropriately. Applies pressures on students quite fairly as well.

Dr. Jones is a great prof.  He's super enthusiastic about pretty much everything he lectures on.  You can get by in the class without reading the textbook, but on the tests there are quite a few questions on the tests on material not covered in lecture, so you're better off reading the text.
A great proff, great man too. you wont regret taking him, just study ahead for his quizzes and his mock tests, they need some attention.
Without a doubt best prof I've had at SFU so far. Lectures are fun, made me love engineering. Take his class even if you're not an engineering major!
really nice guy easy B guranteed. Never attended his lectures just went home and studied instead but overall this course brings your gpa up
John Jones is the most interesting man in the world. But, in all seriousness, extremely interesting to listen to, amazing course, and you can tell he loves to talk about it.
Great professor! I took his class my first term at SFU and really helped me start out on a good footing. His lectures are so fun and interesting, they are the only ones I goto!
awesome teacher love his shoes
One of the best professors at SFU. Even if you aren't an ENSC major you should try to take his course. He's awesome.
Excellent prof. the combination of good personality and high knowledge. I love him
extremely helpful, fair  and knowledgeable
Excellent teacher. Very smart guy. Love the accent. His lectures are very interesting. Reading the book helps a lot for the quizes. Overall a very good professor.
My favourite course in the engineering program. I learned so many interesting things in this class. Highly recommended even if you're not in the program
the lectures are boring..just read the text book
He is a nice and helpful, while at the same time an interesting professor who makes the course fun.

Teaches with wit, hands, and interesting slides and videos. Supposed to have come for a 10 minute presentation and he grilled us for 25! I think he really liked it and wanted to know more! Very approachable. Liked to 1st class where he broke us up into our tutorial groups for the semester.
It was good in the beginning of the year when it was history, not anymore though...
AWESOME TEACHER, I love his British accent, make it really easy to listen to.

My favourite prof. Very interesting lectures on a myriad of engineering topics. He is a great speaker, witty with a good sense of humour. 3 quizzes instead of a final. Pay attention and study his notes to get a pretty easy A.

I heard this class was easy... but it definitely isn't. 3 quizzes instead of a final, and most of the questions required deep understanding.. I couldn't just attend lecture and read the notes; still did terribly.. otherwise he's an interesting prof

Very clever wit, introduces a ton of new ideas with clarity. Added many guest speakers on many subjects that I didn't know I would be interested in! I'm looking forward to any other classes that I may have with him. He made me think in a new way about everyday things.

very nice prof. as long as you speng a little time you'll get an A. this is the easiest course you could possibly encounter in engineering, if you have difficulty in this course then I recommand you to not continue with engineerin. use this course well to boost up your gpa and good luck.
Nice guy, enjoys teaching, even comes out to student activities (paintballing).  Lectures are kind of a joke, but what do you expect when he is teaching a filler course.
Awesome Prof. Welcomes you whole heartedly as a 1st yr student. Go to the lectures for fun. Read them before the final. U'll get an A
great ever

He is an excellent man and a very helpful instructor. If you want to borrow his trancparencies or video cassettes, he deffinitely gives them to you. The final exam is not easy; try studying the lecture notes during the term. Good Luck!
kick ass prof...best prof u can prbly have.

The best teacher ever...
 John Jones Rocks...
very good
It's alright.
Very good prof and an excellent lecturer
very good prof.!!!
We'll miss you Jonesy

He's many engineering students' introduction to university and for that role, he is not a bad choice. Lectures are clear and easy to follow, and the topics chosen are varied and interesting enough to get students interested for the rest of the degree.
Quizzes were too broad which made it really difficult to study for. The persuasive paper is 40% of your mark so spend a lot of time on that. He's a pretty funny professor though.

Mike grades on a curve. I did well on the paper which meant I did well in the class. The quizzes were tough and the average was low, but the curve boosted me. Attend the lectures and read the textbook and youll get a good grade. The group project is easy as well.

Lectures are okay, but don't teach you enough to do well in the class. If it wasn't mandatory and graded, I'd say stay home and read the text book. Honestly, I got the second highest mark on the midterm by just binge-reading the textbook in the week before. The average was about half of my grade. Decent teacher, but the text is more useful.

I enjoyed Mike's class a lot, he is an engaging lecturer and has a good sense of humour. The group project will become tedious but it was a good experience nonetheless. The final paper is essential to doing well, so make sure you put in the effort. Quizzes are based on readings AND lectures, he'll give hints in lecture on what will be on the quiz.

The first 'Group Project' class of engineering. However... The persuasive paper is worth 40% of your grade. Start thinking about what you want to write early, and FOLLOW THE RUBRIC. Seriously. The paper's worth double the entire group project.

Goated Prof and gives good feedback and has good sense of humour. Lectures are clear and very interesting. Make sure to attend lectures and pay lots of attention because the things he talks about in lectures are on quizzes. Also do practice quizzes he provides and take good notes. Definitely recommend 10/10.
The actual best first year ensc professor.

Course is graded by two quizzes which define your mark, along with a design lab and a paper. I had a pleasant time in his class, but pay attention to his lectures as most of the material on the quiz are based on what he's saying.

Course is graded by two quizzes which define your mark, along with a design lab and a paper. I had a pleasant time in his class, but pay attention to his lectures as most of the material on the quiz are based on what he's saying.

Nothing notable about lectures, they were generally straightforward and easy to follow. Quizzes are fairly simple and follow common sense. Group project grade depends mostly on your TA rather than Mike.

Mike is funny and the overall class is not bad, make sure to do practice quizzes as he uses a lot of old questions for his quizzes. also make sure to take good notes because the lecture slides he posts aren't very helpful by itself if you are trying to study

Lecture slides are mostly just pictures and quizzes are very reliant on what he says in class. Worth mentioning that half of the lectures in the term were guest lectures. Gives good feedback and does try to remember a lot of students' names. Engaging and very reachable and responsive, generous too.

Lecture slides are mostly just pictures and quizzes are very reliant on what he says in class. Worth mentioning that half of the lectures in the term were guest lectures. Gives good feedback and does try to remember a lot of students' names. Engaging and very reachable and responsive, generous too.
Enjoyed my semester with him. Make sure you do the previous years quizzes, almost the exact same as the ones in class (Same questions).

Mike Hegedus is a very nice man, he is funny and his lectures are entertaining. The lectures involve history of engineering and society, with guest lectures on topics such as "Space engineering" and "Military engineering". The labs are where you work with your group to design and build an engineering project that solves a problem. Study for quizes!

Mike Hegedus is a very nice man, he is funny and his lectures are entertaining. The lectures involve history of engineering and society, with guest lectures on topics such as "Space engineering" and "Military engineering". The labs are where you work with your group to design and build an engineering project that solves a problem. Study for quizes!

Pay attention and take lots of notes. Much of the quiz content is not on the slides so you must go off what he is saying. For the group project go to his office hours often to discuss things with him, he is good at helping with problems you may encounter. Overall a nice and fair professor.

Mike is a cool guy to be around. His subject isn't super interesting at times, but just make sure to take notes anyway because you'll need it to study for quizzes. The practice quizzes he posts don't have answer keys attached to them, so make detailed notes. It's easy to mess up on his quizzes. He's a pretty nice guy to talk to, and is funny too.

Mike is awesome. Although he can seem very rough around the edges and critical, he genuinely cares about his Eng student's success. Come to him for advice and he will always be willing to talk, and he is very accessible outside the class. The lectures cover all material for the quizzes, and as long as you take notes you'll be fine.
He is the most boring person ever. If u have him make sure u bring airpods to class.

Goated professor. Had him for ENSC 100 in my first semester at SFU, he was always helpful and accessible for questions I had about other classes as well. Assignments and lectures were good, and quizzes were pretty difficult, but overall a pretty good course.
Always there to help, even if the assignment isn't from his class lol.
One of the best professors you can have. ENSC 100W was the highlight of my day with Mike.
The only good professor in first year engineering.
Mike Hegedus was a decent professor, but he made some inappropriate comments during a lecture that nauseated me.

Mike is a wonderful prof who truly cares about his students. I actually look forward to his lectures, and they're always the highlight of my day. It should be noted that he does not record his lectures and that attendance is an absolute must.

Mike is honestly really awesome. As a first-year engineering student, he really helped prepare us for the workload, giving us a timeline for when things would get tough (ie, when heavy work load begins). He's always there to talk to, even if its just general engineering stuff, not course related.

Mike is the real og. If anyone talks smack on here about him, I'll be seeing you in the back of a Wendy's. There's not much in this class other than a project and a paper, so if you got a good group you're fine. Mike rocks my socks off, he cares about his students and leaves you teary at the end of the semester. Mike is the best, lest we forgest.

Steve is great. Gave out candy on multiple occasions, and is an all-around good lecturer. Participating in the class is 20% of your grade so show up and comment once every week or so in the discussion boards. Passing this class is not difficult.
